title: Staged quality throttle and autorevert engine for config/model flips
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a staged exposure controller that monitors evaluation signals during small-scale config or model changes and automatically throttles traffic or reverts the change when statistically significant quality degradation is detected. This ticket covers the runtime controller logic, evaluation gating rules, orchestration hooks to update routing policies, and a small console surface for observability and manual override.
background: We frequently ship model/config changes that can have subtle regressions for specific cohorts. Manual canaries are slow and error-prone. Existing rollout primitives route traffic but lack a compact evaluation engine that ties statistical tests and business-quality signals to automated traffic reduction and safe reversion. This feature aims to reduce time-to-detection and human toil while minimizing customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Controller receives staged-release events and attaches an evaluation window to the cohort
Controller executes pre-configured evaluation bundles (metrics + tests) and computes effect sizes with p-values or sequential test bounds
If degradation exceeds thresholds for two consecutive windows, controller reduces cohort traffic by pre-configured steps and triggers a recorded revert if thresholds persist after throttle
Console shows per-cohort evaluation summary, primary/secondary metrics, decision timeline, and allows manual override (pause, force-commit, force-revert)
Latency and cost overhead of evaluation plumbing is <3% for normal traffic and isolated to canary cohorts
E2E smoke tests covering: happy path commit, transient blip (recovers), and persistent regression (auto-revert)
design_decisions: Use stratified sampling to ensure the eval cohort mirrors production user slices (region, plan, route)
Prefer sequential hypothesis testing (e.g., alpha-spending) over repeated independent p-values to avoid inflated false positives during rolling windows
Primary signal is a weighted quality score (combination of BLEU-like task-specific metric + business KPIs), secondary signals include latency percentile and error-rate
Controller exposes an extensible plugin interface to add new eval transforms (embedding drift, hallucination detectors)
Traffic reduction steps: 50% -> 10% -> 0% with configurable hold windows between steps
Fallback hierarchy: reduce traffic -> switch to compatible model variant -> revert config change (in that order)
metrics: Primary_quality_delta: absolute drop >= 3% AND relative drop >= 5% triggers alert
95th_latency_delta: increase > 200ms for two windows is considered a degradation signal
Error_rate: > 0.5% absolute increase is high impact for high-volume routes
Statistical confidence: sequential test reaches 95% confidence bound before decisive action
Customer_impact_tagging: cohorts with 'high' customer_impact have lower thresholds for action
plan: Spec: 3 days - finalize thresholds, window sizing, sampling rules and API contract with Console/Router teams
Runtime: 8 days - implement controller, sequential test library, router hooks for traffic steering
Observability: 3 days - dashboards, traces, eval artifacts storage retention policy
QA: 2 days - integration tests with dedicated and hosted modes
Rollout: gradual internal rollout -> opt-in beta customers -> default behavior behind feature flag
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): enable controller in dev cluster with synthetic traffic and canary model variants
Stage 1 (beta): opt-in customers for non-critical routes, monitor for false positives for 2 weeks
Stage 2 (pilot): default enabled for low-traffic routes with conservative thresholds
Stage 3 (GA): enable on most routes with user-facing console controls and documented runbook
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: controller-decision-failed -> SEV2 if evaluation job fails to complete within window
Alert: unexpected-revert -> SEV1 if auto-revert fires for >3 distinct routes in 1 hour
Dashboard: per-release timeline with metric deltas and decision annotations
Audit log: every automatic action writes an immutable event (release-id, window, metric-delta, decision, actor)
runbook: If controller triggers throttle: verify metric deltas in console; if transient, mark window as flaky and resume rollout
If controller auto-reverts: notify SRE and release owner, open postmortem if customer-impact is high
If controller fails to compute test: fallback to traffic-steering policy (route to safe variant) and retry evaluation job
Manual override steps: Console -> Release -> Pause or Force Revert (requires two-person auth for high-impact cohorts)
